comment: Two surveys of maintenance staff report use at about 27% and 18%. They disagree on whether the 25% line is crossed, so the cautious level is set. Both surveys are from companies in the maintenance business. Not AI-specific. Pages checked by the owner.

source: Axis Communications customer story on BMW Group
comment: BMW's AIQX system: camera-based AI quality checks, said to run in all BMW Group plants. The source is the camera supplier, not BMW. AI-specific. A Rockwell survey reports that 50% of manufacturers plan AI for quality in 2025, which is intent, not use. Page checked by the owner.

source: ARC Advisory Group survey (via Siemens blog)
comment: 33% of participating companies have implemented digital twin and simulation technology, above the 25% line. Other surveys report 20% to 29% depending on the definition. Not AI-specific. Page checked by the owner.

BMW i8 Roadster roof bracket: designed with topology optimisation software and 3D printed in metal, in mass production at low volumes. The source is from 2018. Topology optimisation, not an AI method as such. Page opened and confirmed by the assistant.

source: International Federation of Robotics, President's Report 2026
comment: 66,000 collaborative robots installed in 2025, 11% of all industrial robot installations. This is a share of installations, not a survey of manufacturers, so it does not meet the rule for level 3. Says nothing about how many use AI. Page opened and confirmed by the assistant.

AI software for controlling cement kilns is offered commercially. A deployment at the Mokra cement plant is reported in search results, but the page could not be opened, so level 2 is not confirmed. AI-specific. Cement industry only. Open point: confirm the named plant, then raise to 2.
